sections.heading: Glossary term: Extinction
sections.body: The reduction in intensity of starlight reaching us is called extinction. This reduction is due to absorption and scattering of light by particles along the path of light. Extinction could be due to Earth's atmosphere (called atmospheric extinction), material in the immediate vicinity of a star (called circumstellar extinction), or due to material between stars in deep space (called interstellar extinction). The atmospheric extinction is mainly due to aerosols and molecules present in Earth's atmosphere such as water, carbon dioxide, and ozone at optical and near-infrared wavelengths. Interstellar extinction is attributed to interstellar matter made up of gas and submicron-sized dust particles. Interstellar dust has a drastic effect on starlight as compared to the gas particles. Extinction is generally higher at shorter wavelengths and vice-versa making astronomical objects appear redder than their true color (reddening).

Glossary term: Extinction

Redirected from Reddening

Description: The reduction in intensity of starlight reaching us is called extinction. This reduction is due to absorption and scattering of light by particles along the path of light. Extinction could be due to Earth's atmosphere (called atmospheric extinction), material in the immediate vicinity of a star (called circumstellar extinction), or due to material between stars in deep space (called interstellar extinction). The atmospheric extinction is mainly due to aerosols and molecules present in Earth's atmosphere such as water, carbon dioxide, and ozone at optical and near-infrared wavelengths. Interstellar extinction is attributed to interstellar matter made up of gas and submicron-sized dust particles. Interstellar dust has a drastic effect on starlight as compared to the gas particles. Extinction is generally higher at shorter wavelengths and vice-versa making astronomical objects appear redder than their true color (reddening).

Related Terms:

  • Atmospheric Extinction
  • Dust
  • Interstellar Extinction


See this term in other languages

Term and definition status: This term and its definition have been approved by a research astronomer and a teacher

The OAE Multilingual Glossary is a project of the IAU Office of Astronomy for Education (OAE) in collaboration with the IAU Office of Astronomy Outreach (OAO). The terms and definitions were chosen, written and reviewed by a collective effort from the OAE, the OAE Centers and Nodes, the OAE National Astronomy Education Coordinators (NAECs) and other volunteers. sections.body_ru: Уменьшение интенсивности звездного света, достигающего нас, называется экстинкцией. Это уменьшение обусловлено поглощением и рассеянием света частицами на пути света. Экстинкция может быть вызвана атмосферой Земли (называемая атмосферной экстинкцией), материалом в непосредственной близости от звезды (называемая околозвездной экстинкцией) или материалом между звездами в глубоком космосе (называемая межзвездной экстинкцией). Атмосферная экстинкция в основном обусловлена аэрозолями и молекулами, присутствующими в атмосфере Земли, такими как вода, углекислый газ и озон, на оптических и ближних инфракрасных длинах волн. Межзвездная экстинкция приписывается межзвездному веществу, состоящему из газа и пылевых частиц субмикронного размера. Межзвездная пыль оказывает резкое влияние на звездный свет по сравнению с газовыми частицами. Экстинкция обычно выше на более коротких длинах волн и наоборот, что заставляет астрономические объекты казаться краснее их истинного цвета (покраснение).
